title: How many missed samples can a PD loop tuned on a fixed-period twin survive?
lede: how many missed samples can a PD loop tuned on a fixed-period twin survive? With samples lost independently and the last command held, a double-integrator loop with twin poles at 0.5 is mean-square stable only up to a 29% loss rate but almost surely stable up to 61%; a deadbeat twin tolerates 7% in mean square.
summary: Double-integrator plant under PD control with zero-order hold; gains place both closed-loop poles of the fixed-period twin at z = r (h0 = 0.1). Each sample is lost independently with probability q, so the interval is m h0 with geometric m. Mean-square stability is an exact 3×3 second-moment operator with a Jury test; almost-sure stability is a Lyapunov exponent from a 200,000-sample product. For r = 0.5 the loop is mean-square stable up to q = 0.293 and almost surely up to 0.611 (999 of 1,000 runs converge at 0.55); deadbeat r = 0 gives 0.070 and 0.753, slow r = 0.9 gives 0.780 and 0.907. The operator matches Monte Carlo where the tails are sampled and a 400,000-run Monte Carlo of the mean square misses it by 6% at q = 0.3. Stylised: one chosen plant and loop, independent losses, no noise, delay or saturation, none taken from a robot or datasheet.
